Answer typed questions about a state

Source: R/predict.R
laya_predict.Rd

laya_predict() answers every question about one state in a single forward pass. laya_predict_batch() does the same for many states. laya_predict_long() scans a state longer than the model's context in overlapping windows and keeps, per question, the most confident window.

Usage

laya_predict(
  state,
  questions,
  engine = laya_default_engine(),
  ...,
  min_confidence = NULL,
  lang = NULL,
  max_len = NULL,
  head_max_len = NULL
)

laya_predict_batch(
  states,
  questions,
  engine = laya_default_engine(),
  ...,
  batch_size = getOption("layaR.batch_size", 1L),
  sort_by_length = FALSE,
  min_confidence = NULL,
  lang = NULL,
  max_len = NULL,
  head_max_len = NULL,
  chunk_size = 64L,
  progress = interactive()
)

laya_predict_long(
  state,
  questions,
  engine = laya_default_engine(),
  ...,
  window = NULL,
  stride = NULL,
  batch_size = NULL,
  lang = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'laya_engine'
predict(object, state, questions, ...)

Arguments

state

A string, a named list, or a one-row data frame.

questions

A question set from laya_questions() or laya_preset(), or anything as_laya_questions() accepts.

engine

A laya_engine(). Defaults to laya_default_engine().

...

Must be empty; the options below are named.

min_confidence

Optional abstention gate: a threshold in [0, 1], or a named numeric vector of thresholds per option-count bucket (names from laya_bucket_keys(), plus "default"). The threshold is compared with each answer's answer_confidence (for a choice question, the chosen option's probability), as in the Python SDK. Every answer then reports abstention: "passed", "abstained" or "unevaluated".

lang

Optional language code (e.g. "fr") selecting per-language calibration temperatures, when the engine has them.

max_len, head_max_len

Optional per-call token budgets overriding the checkpoint's: the whole sequence, and the part spent on a question's options.

states

A character vector, a list of states, or a data frame (each row becomes a named list).

batch_size

States per forward pass. Defaults to the layaR.batch_size option, or 1: on a CPU, one state per pass is usually fastest, because a batch pads every state to the longest one (see vignette("models-and-performance", package = "layaR")). Larger batches can pay off on other hardware. NULL sends each chunk in one pass, as the Python SDK does by default. Results are the same either way.

sort_by_length

Group similarly sized states within a chunk to reduce padding (only with a batch_size above 1 and smaller than the chunk).

chunk_size

States sent to the engine per call. Between chunks R can be interrupted and the progress bar updates.

progress

Show a progress bar? Defaults to TRUE in interactive sessions with more than one chunk.

window, stride

Optional scan window and stride, in tokens. By default the window is the room the questions leave in one sequence and the stride is half the window.

object

A laya_engine, for the stats::predict() method.

Value

laya_predict() and laya_predict_long() return a laya_result; laya_predict_batch() returns a laya_batch_result (a list of laya_results, in input order). See laya_result for how to read them.

Details

A state is either a single string, used verbatim, or a named list, which the model reads as a JSON object (field order is kept). A one-row data frame is read as a named list.

Examples

if (laya_model_available()) {
  qs <- laya_questions(
    department = laya_choice("Which department should handle this?",
                             billing = "invoices, refunds",
                             technical = "bugs, outages"),
    churn_risk = laya_noul("Does the user threaten to cancel?")
  )
  res <- laya_predict("I was billed twice. Refund me or I cancel.", qs)
  res
  as.data.frame(res)

  laya_predict_batch(c("Refund please", "The app crashes"), qs)
}
